subject: Short-term capacity cushion request for BrightScale rollout
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightscale.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@brightscale.com
Date: 2028-06-16T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Short-term capacity cushion for BrightScale rollout

Hi Michael,

Quick background — BrightScale is launching a new personalization feature on July 1 and based on our load tests we expect a concentrated peak during the first 72 hours. We're committed to your committed tier today but will likely exceed our monthly allocation briefly.

Can Redwood provide a short-term capacity cushion (temporary quota increase / traffic buffer) to absorb spikes for ~2–3 weeks? Key questions:
- What are the pricing options for a temporary cushion (prepay vs post-pay true-up)?
- Can we get any discount for an emergency buffer tied to a committed expansion?
- How will billing show up — one-off invoice, pro-rated true-up, or an overrun line item?

Goal is to avoid throttling during rollout while keeping predictable invoicing for our finance team. If useful, procurement copied here and I can share forecast numbers.

Thanks — appreciate any quick options/ballpark.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform, BrightScale
liam.oconnor@brightscale.com
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brightscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-16T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity cushion for BrightScale rollout

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the rollout. We can absolutely put a transient buffer in place to prevent throttles. Two straightforward options that we typically offer:

1) Prepay cushion (fastest): you buy a prepaid buffer pool (tokens/min) for the window. We invoice up front; unused portion can be credited toward the next month. We can offer a 20% discount off our standard overrun rate if you prepay for the full 21-day window.

2) Post-pay true-up (simpler for procurement): we enable a temporary quota increase for up to 21 days, meter consumption, and true-up after the window. For this route we recommend a modest cap on daily invoicing to protect both sides. Discount here normally is smaller (10–15%).

Practical proposal for BrightScale (based on your note): a 21-day cushion that increases your throughput by 100k tokens/minute. Option A (prepay): 20% off overrun rate, one up-front invoice. Option B (post-pay): 15% discount, daily cap of $8,000 on overrun charges, true-up after the 21 day window.

I've attached a quick quote and a capacity addendum template for sign-off. Can you confirm preferred option and whether procurement wants a PO before we enable the buffer? If you'd like, I can loop in our billing lead (Marissa) to align on invoice flow and Ben on contractual language.

Best,
Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
Attachments: BrightScale_cushion_quote_v1.pdf, SOW_redwood_template.pdf
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-16T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Short-term capacity cushion for BrightScale rollout — internal pricing check

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Liam's ask. My proposed external language above; quick internal notes and questions:

— I suggested 20% off if they prepay for 21 days, or 15% post-pay with an $8k/day cap.
— Marissa: if we prepay with 20% off, do we need to automatically credit unused tokens proportionally? I suggested we offer credit toward next invoice.
— Ben: on the post-pay option, procurement may push back on daily caps. Would we prefer a weekly cap instead? Also, any concerns on exposure with a 100k tokens/min buffer?

Appended previous message for context. Would like to respond to them today.

—Michael

Date: 2028-06-18T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity cushion for BrightScale rollout — agreement and next steps

Liam / procurement team — thanks for the quick responses earlier. BrightScale, glad to confirm final terms so we can enable the cushion tomorrow morning UTC: 

Scope: enable a temporary capacity cushion that increases BrightScale's throughput by 100,000 tokens/minute for 21 calendar days starting 2028-06-20 00:00 UTC.

Billing & discount: we agreed to the post-pay true-up route. Key billing items:
- Discount: 15% off the standard overrun rate for cushion consumption during the 21-day window.
- Cap: Redwood will cap daily overrun invoicing at $8,000/day. Any usage beyond that will be discussed and handled as an escalation; we will notify BrightScale by email when usage approaches the cap.
- True-up: consumption metered daily, invoice issued 7 days after the window ends (single true-up invoice).

Attachments: I attached an updated capacity addendum (BrightScale_capacity_addendum.pdf) that mirrors the bullets above and a quote. Please sign the addendum via DocuSign at the link below; we will not enable the buffer until we receive a signed addendum or a procurement exception.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/contract/abc123-quicksign
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BS-4721

If procurement prefers prepay instead, we can swap to Option A (20% off with up-front invoice and credit for unused pool) — let me know. Otherwise we will enable the post-pay cushion on 2028-06-20 at 00:00 UTC once the signed addendum is back.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth launch.

—Michael
Michael Grant
